title: Operate, Recover, and Improve Agent Systems
summary: Classify failures across the full agent stack, contain impact, reconcile uncertain actions, recover safely, and turn incidents into verified improvements.
objectives: Distinguish model, prompt, tool, retrieval, data, policy, orchestration, and infrastructure failures.
Triage severity and contain unsafe action, data exposure, cost, and cascading retries.
Recover with reconciliation, idempotency, rollback, replay, and human escalation.
Convert operational evidence into tests, controls, runbook updates, and measured improvement.

sections.title: Classify the failed boundary before changing the model
paragraphs: Model failures include unsupported or incorrect generation. Prompt failures encode ambiguous or conflicting behavior. Tool failures include bad contracts, authorization, execution, or postconditions. Retrieval and data failures include missing, stale, poisoned, malformed, or cross-tenant evidence.

Policy failures allow forbidden action or block required escalation. Orchestration failures misroute, loop, race, or lose state. Infrastructure failures include capacity, network, dependency, credential, storage, and deployment faults. Several classes can occur in one incident, so record evidence instead of forcing one convenient cause.

sections.title: Triage impact and contain first
paragraphs: Assess affected users, tenants, data, permissions, external actions, money, availability, and legal or safety obligations. Set severity from actual and credible potential impact, not from how fluent the agent output looks.

Contain by pausing the workflow or one tool, revoking credentials, disabling a route, reducing concurrency, switching to a safe fallback, or requiring manual approval. Preserve secret-safe traces, configuration versions, request IDs, and postcondition evidence before mutable state disappears.
sections.callout: When the real-world outcome is unknown, do not classify the action as failed and retry it blindly.

sections.title: Reconcile before retry, rollback, or replay
paragraphs: A transport timeout does not prove that a write failed. Query the system of record with an idempotency key or correlation ID, compare the intended and actual postcondition, then choose accept, compensate, retry, rollback, or escalate.

Retry only transient failures with exponential backoff, jitter, provider guidance, and a total budget. Do not retry validation, authorization, policy, or deterministic conflict failures unchanged. Roll back through a tested reversible path and verify the restored state.

code.label: Recovery decision
code.code:
if outcome == UNKNOWN: reconcile system_of_record
if unauthorized or policy_blocked: stop + escalate
if transient and retry_budget > 0: backoff + idempotent retry
if harmful change and rollback_tested: rollback + verify
otherwise: preserve evidence + human decision

sections.title: Give responders a decision-ready runbook
paragraphs: A runbook names triggers, severity, owner, communication channel, dashboards and queries, containment choices, credentials and approvals, reconciliation steps, rollback or fallback, validation, escalation, and closure criteria. Commands should be safe to copy and explicit about targets.

Status updates distinguish confirmed facts, hypotheses, actions, impact, and next decision. Notify affected people under the organization's incident and privacy obligations without exposing secrets or unsupported blame.

sections.title: Close only after recovery evidence and prevention work
paragraphs: Verify user-visible recovery, external postconditions, queues and retries, permissions, data isolation, cost, and monitoring. A green health endpoint alone may miss incomplete work or a duplicated side effect.

Write a blameless timeline and contributing factors, add the smallest reproducing case to the evaluation suite, improve the control at the failed boundary, rehearse the changed runbook, and measure recurrence. Track follow-up work to completion rather than treating the post-incident review as closure.

activity.title: Triage and recover a multi-boundary agent incident
instructions: Use a scenario where an agent times out after a consequential tool call, retrieves stale data, and produces an unsupported completion claim.
Build a timeline and classify model, prompt, tool, retrieval, data, policy, orchestration, and infrastructure evidence without assuming one root cause.
Write the severity, containment, reconciliation, retry, rollback, communication, escalation, validation, and closure steps.
Convert the incident into regression cases, a control change, a runbook rehearsal, an owner, and a recurrence metric.
evidence: A failure-classification matrix, incident timeline, impact and severity decision, and executable triage/recovery runbook.
Reconciliation and rollback evidence plus tracked evaluation, control, rehearsal, and monitoring improvements.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which symptom looked like a model failure until the trace exposed a different failed boundary?

cues.text: Classify model, prompt, tool, retrieval, data, policy, orchestration, and infrastructure evidence before choosing a fix.

Reconcile unknown outcomes before bounded retry, compensation, rollback, replay, or escalation.
Move an uncertain tool action through contain, reconcile, decide, recover, verify, and close states.

cues.text: Use a target-specific runbook and communicate confirmed facts, hypotheses, impact, actions, and required decisions separately.
Close after user-visible recovery, then turn the incident into regression tests, control changes, rehearsal, and recurrence measures.
Ask learners why a timeout after a write must be classified as unknown rather than failed.
Allow three minutes to add one exact rollback target and one human escalation trigger.
Check that closure proves the external postcondition and assigns every prevention action.
Guide failure classification, containment, reconciliation, rollback, communication, and prevention work.
Begin the check after the learner can recover without duplicate impact or unsupported completion claims.

questions.prompt: An agent gives the wrong answer because the retriever returned an expired policy. What is the primary failed boundary?
questions.explanation: The evidence source was stale; changing model wording would not repair the failed retrieval/data boundary.

questions.prompt: A write request times out after reaching the server. What should happen before retry?
choices: Reconcile the idempotency key and actual postcondition
questions.explanation: The outcome is unknown until the system of record proves whether the side effect occurred.

questions.prompt: Which failure should not be retried unchanged?
choices: A connection reset before any request
questions.explanation: Deterministic validation and authorization failures require corrected input or authority, not repetition.

questions.prompt: What is the first priority when an agent may still be taking unsafe actions?
choices: Contain the workflow or affected capability
questions.explanation: Containment limits ongoing impact before diagnosis and long-term remediation.

questions.prompt: Which failure map correctly separates system boundaries?
choices: Unsupported claim: model; conflicting instruction: prompt; bad action contract: tool; stale source: retrieval or data; forbidden action: policy; provider outage: infrastructure
Every failure is a model failure
A provider outage is a prompt failure and stale data is infrastructure
Authorization and tool execution are the same as output style
questions.explanation: Useful triage identifies the first failed boundary instead of treating every symptom as a model problem.
